title: The Asset of Marseille's old port
premise: Odile Nystrom, a deniable fixer for an embassy that exists on no map, discovers their Marseille safe house listed on a real-estate site — every room photographed, including the wall of case files they thought was hidden. The listing is a message from Vasseur, the handler who trained them and now sells the network piece by piece. With dawn extraction as a hard deadline, Odile must decide whether to flee clean or burn the training program that made them, dragging along Tomas Reyes, the analyst they were ordered to abandon and cannot. They burn it, at the cost of the network's last safe exit, and board the flight with nothing but each other and a memory they chose to keep.
about_author: Jude Ravensworth is the pen name of a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade auditing cargo that officially never moved through Mediterranean ports. They write from a rented flat above a shuttered chandlery, and refuse to confirm which parts are invented.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Odile. Scrolling property listings over coffee, Odile finds the safe house for sale — photos of the interior, the file wall, the second toothbrush. The emotional beat is cold recognition: someone inside did this. They photograph the screen back, a signal to whoever is watching, and begin counting exits.

chapters.title: Vasseur's Grammar
chapters.summary: POV: Odile. Decoding the listing as a message: the photo angles match Vasseur's old training exercises, his way of saying 'I own you still.' Flashbacks braid with present fear. Beat: the horror of realizing your oldest teacher is your active threat, and that obedience was trained deeper than loyalty.

chapters.title: Reyes
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas Reyes. The analyst arrives unannounced, sent by the same phantom embassy, carrying orders to archive everything and abandon Odile if compromised. He hesitates at the door. Beat: two people trained never to trust, choosing to anyway — love beginning as an act of insubordination.

chapters.title: Old Port, New Buyers
chapters.summary: POV: Odile. Working the Vieux-Port contacts, Odile learns three buyers have viewed the house — all fronts for services wanting the network's methods. A meet goes wrong; a courier dies badly. Beat: the sale isn't fiction, it's an auction, and Odile is lot number one.

chapters.title: What the Training Made
chapters.summary: POV: Reyes. Reading the archived files, Reyes reconstructs what was done to Odile — the drills, the erasures, the loyalty tests disguised as betrayals. He says nothing of the worst page. Beat: tenderness curdling into complicity; he now holds power over the person he loves.

chapters.title: The Counteroffer
chapters.summary: POV: Odile. Vasseur makes contact in person at a fish market: retire quietly, or the full dossier goes to the buyers at midnight. He offers Odile partnership — the corruption dressed as inheritance. Beat: temptation played straight; the offer is genuinely good, which is what makes it monstrous.

chapters.title: Burn List
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Odile and Reyes draft the plan to torch the program: servers in a bank cellar, a judge on retainer, six names including Vasseur's. Reyes confesses he read the worst page. Beat: rupture and repair — trust rebuilt not by hiding damage but by showing it.

chapters.title: Midnight Auction
chapters.summary: POV: Odile. The buyers convene; Vasseur presents the dossier. Odile infiltrates as a bidder's aide, planting the evidence that turns the buyers against each other while Reyes triggers the fire alarms and data purge upstairs. Beat: rising chaos, competence under pressure, first blood.

chapters.title: The Cellar
chapters.summary: POV: Reyes. Climax. Confronting Vasseur among the burning servers, Reyes offers him the choice Odile never got: die as the program or live as a man. Vasseur chooses the program. Odile arrives too late to stop it, in time to pull Reyes out. Beat: power's final corruption — a man who would rather burn than be ordinary.

chapters.title: Dawn Flight
chapters.summary: POV: Odile. Ash over the Vieux-Port, the network dead, no clean exit left — only a cargo flight and forged papers for two. Odile keeps one photograph from the file wall: themselves at twelve, before. Beat: grief and release; love chosen over duty, memory kept by will rather than training, wheels up as the sun rises.
